speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing both psychiatric symptoms and a new movement disorder. To begin our assessment, can you describe the specific changes in your mood or behavior that you are noticing?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is good to hear regarding your psychiatric improvement. However, since you are also experiencing a new movement disorder, have you noticed any stiffness, tremors, or involuntary muscle contractions since starting Risperidone?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—pacing, fidgeting, and an inability to remain still—are classic signs of akathisia. Given your recent start on risperidone, this is a likely side effect. How severe is this restlessness on a scale of 1 to 10, and is it interfering significantly with your daily activities or sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming your history; the absence of substance use helps isolate the medication as the cause. How severe is this restlessness on a scale of 1 to 10, and is it significantly interfering with your sleep or ability to function?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced akathisia secondary to risperidone use.
